description: Catalog of every credential the investigation pipeline knows how to use. Each entry maps to a `name` checked by core.research.credentials.get_credential(): same key for the secrets table row AND the env-var fallback. The wizard step 6 UI reads this list to know what to ask for; the status endpoint stamps each entry with `configured: true/false`. When `configured`, source handlers bump rate limits and unlock per-source data paths described in `unlocks`. Open source — every operator picks which keys their server runs with; no commercial tier branding.

credentials.name: DATA_GOV_API_KEY
credentials.label: data.gov API key
unlocks: FEC donor money-trail (top 20 individual contributions per campaign)
FEC principal committee → donor cascade
Congress.gov member lookup (politicians, committees)
FDA OpenFDA at 240/min instead of polite-poll
credentials.without_key: FEC runs candidate+committee search only at DEMO_KEY rate; Congress returns no_api_key; FDA still works but throttled.
credentials.notes: One key unlocks three sources. Highest leverage free key.

credentials.name: SAM_GOV_API_KEY
credentials.label: SAM.gov API key
unlocks: Federal contractor entity records (UEI, CAGE, registration status)
Vendor capability statements and POC contacts
Cross-reference with USAspending awards
credentials.without_key: Returns no_api_key status; no contractor data ingested.
credentials.notes: Hard 10/day public ceiling — effectively requires a key for any real use.

credentials.name: GEONAMES_USERNAME
credentials.label: GeoNames username
unlocks: Alternate names for cities/places (Tehran ↔ TEHRAN ↔ Тегеран)
Population, admin hierarchy, feature class
Resolves case-variant entity collisions at admit time
credentials.without_key: GeoNames source skipped; place admissions rely on Wikipedia + Nominatim only.
credentials.notes: Username (not API key). Must enable 'web services' on your GeoNames profile after signup — easily missed.

credentials.name: OPENCORPORATES_API_TOKEN
credentials.label: OpenCorporates API token
unlocks: Per-company /officers endpoint (full director board, not just first page)
Full corporate empire mapping for persons (officer roles across all jurisdictions)
Higher result page cap (25 → 100 per query)
Subsidiary chain traversal
credentials.without_key: Bulk search works at 500/day; per-company /officers skipped to stay under quota; deep corporate maps incomplete.
credentials.notes: Biggest data unlock per dollar for entity investigation. Director chains beyond the first OpenCorporates page require this.

credentials.name: OPENSANCTIONS_API_KEY
credentials.label: OpenSanctions API key
credentials.free_rate: Bulk download only; per-name lookup unavailable
credentials.keyed_rate: Live per-name API with PEP categories and consolidated dataset
unlocks: Real-time per-name sanctions lookup (no bulk download required)
PEP (politically exposed person) categorization and family-of-PEP detection
Crime + crime-watchlist categories beyond OFAC/UN coverage
Topic-level categorization (corruption, military, oligarch)
credentials.without_key: We rely on OFAC + UN consolidated for designations; PEP / corruption / oligarch tagging missing.
credentials.notes: Best signal for non-US-centric exposure (UK FCDO, EU, AU, CH lists, etc.).

credentials.name: FAA_REGISTRY_BULK_ENABLED
credentials.label: FAA bulk registry cache
credentials.keyed_rate: Reverse search: 'all aircraft owned by X' via local MASTER CSV cache
unlocks: Reverse lookup: list every aircraft registered to a person/org
Aircraft type breakdown per owner
Registration-history timeline
credentials.without_key: Only direct N-number lookup works (when a tail is mentioned in a signal).
credentials.notes: Free but requires nightly download + parse of 70 MB FAA MASTER CSV. Set to 'true' once the cache job is wired.

credentials.name: COMPANIES_HOUSE_API_KEY
credentials.label: UK Companies House API key
unlocks: UK officer (director/secretary) lookup — directorships, fellow directors
UK company search — filings, status, addresses, incorporation date
Disambiguation signals for UK entities (DOB, address) that the disambiguator uses to confirm right-person matches
Officer appointment history (every company a person has been a director of)
credentials.without_key: UK Companies House source returns no_data; British entities have no UK-specific structured data beyond Wikipedia/Wikidata.
credentials.notes: Free, ~5 min to sign up. Single highest-value key for any UK or UK-resident entity. The signup flow asks for an application name — 'Enki Command Center' is fine. Create a live key (not test) for production. Pairs with jurisdiction-routing: source is only invoked for entities the routing flags as British, so it doesn't eat quota on US dossiers.

credentials.name: PROPUBLICA_NONPROFITS_API_KEY
credentials.label: ProPublica Nonprofits API key
credentials.free_rate: Generous, no key required for basic use
unlocks: Bulk 990 filing pulls per nonprofit
Higher-throughput cascade for boards-of-directors networks
credentials.without_key: Works fine for normal investigation rates; only matters for backfill / cascade-heavy runs.
credentials.notes: Optional — leave blank for most operators.

_principles: Open source: no commercial tier; each operator decides which keys to add.
Adding a key MUST take effect within ~30s (no restart). The credentials cache TTL is short by design.
Sources behave at the highest tier available at call time — they re-check on every call so a key added mid-run takes effect immediately.
All values stay server-side. The list endpoint shows configured/not-configured but never reveals values.
Free keys (data.gov, SAM.gov, GeoNames) deliver outsized value — recommend all operators fill them.
